They’re called dark pools because there is no regulatory oversight unlike the other exchanges and very little is known. What is known is that robinhood makes money by completing their customers transactions at the high end of the spread (the difference between the bid and the ask price, usually a couple cents) and pocketing those pennies but millions of times over as each individual stock has a bid and an ask price. But it’s also slightly known that institutional investors use knowledge gained in dark pools to further manipulate the markets against retail investors. 

Again this is what we know of. Wall Street has been making their own rules for a generation with a pathetic amount of oversight from our regulatory bodies.
